topic: Your brain: 2% of your weight, 20% of your energy, 12 watts

sources.title: How much energy does your brain require?
Does Thinking Really Hard Burn More Calories?
Do People Only Use 10 Percent of Their Brains?

claims.text: The brain is about 2% of body weight.
claims.quote: which is about 2% of the total body weight; Your brain accounts for roughly two percent of your body weight

claims.text: The brain uses about 20% of the body's energy at rest.
claims.quote: The brain consumes up to 20% of the energy used by the human body, more than any other organ; it demands 20 percent of our resting metabolic rate; it consumes about 20% of the total energy in the body at rest
20% of total body oxygen consumption; the human brain accounts for about 20% of the total oxygen consumption when a person is at rest
it receives 15% of the cardiac output

claims.text: A typical adult brain runs on about 12 watts, a fifth of a 60-watt bulb.
claims.quote: So a typical adult human brain runs on around 12 watts—a fifth of the power required by a standard 60 watt lightbulb
claims.label: Scientific American's estimate

claims.text: Extra mental effort adds little next to the brain's baseline use.
claims.quote: any local increases in energy consumption are tiny compared with the brain's gluttonous baseline intake; short periods of additional mental effort require a little more brainpower than usual, but not much more

claims.text: Using only 10% of the brain is a myth.
claims.quote: nor that normal humans use only ten per cent of the brain; the "10 percent myth" is so wrong it is almost laughable

myths.myth: You only use 10% of your brain.
myths.truth: A myth: the energy bill alone shows it.
